bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Payment delays and working capital stress from state government receivables — The Company continues to face significant outstanding receivables from state government entities, particularly in Telangana's irrigation sector. Delays on projects such as Kaleshwaram Package 4 have stalled debtor recoveries and increased pressure on working capital. Mitigation is limited to rigorous follow-up and meetings with senior finance and irrigation officials, so the exposure remains structural to a business whose clients are almost entirely government bodies.
- Execution roadblocks from land acquisition and statutory clearances — Project execution is often hindered by delays in land acquisition and statutory approvals including environmental and forest clearances. The mine projects require forest clearance and Gram Sabha approval, while certain road projects have encountered local protests restricting site access. This risk has grown in weight now that mining is the largest single block of the order book at 41%.
- Margin compression from intense competitive bidding — Intense competition in the infrastructure sector has prompted aggressive bidding at lower prices to secure new orders, and management states the highly competitive environment has compressed EBITDA margins compared with historical levels. The Threats column of the SCOT analysis names a highly competitive bidding landscape that forces lower pricing, impacting sustainable margins and growth.
- Commodity price volatility in bitumen and petroleum-linked inputs — Global geopolitical tensions can trigger sharp increases in crude oil prices, driving up the cost of bitumen and other petroleum-based construction inputs, creating uncertainty in project cost management and affecting profitability. Mitigation rests on the revised MoRTH price adjustment mechanism, which shortens the adjustment cycle from three months to one month and enables faster pass-through.
- Liquidity strain and capital concentration in completed assets — Large infrastructure projects require substantial upfront equity investment, pressuring liquidity if capital is not recycled efficiently, and excess capital tied up in completed assets limits the ability to pursue new and diversified opportunities. The response is asset monetisation through divestment of completed HAM assets to infrastructure trusts and reinvestment of proceeds into the order book.
- Dependence on the pace of government project awarding — National highway construction activity declined during 2025-26 and, per the CARE Report cited in the MD&A, is expected to moderate further in 2026-27, from around 25 km per day to 21-22 km per day, on subdued project awarding. Fewer road projects came to tender than in any recent season and management states the year's results reflect that shortfall, so revenue is directly exposed to a policy-driven awarding cycle the Company does not control.
- Client and activity concentration — BRSR Section A records a single business activity, Construction and Engineering, at 100% of turnover, with exports at 0.00% and operations in seven states, all ongoing projects located across South and East India. Sales to related parties were 30.95% of total sales in 2025-26 (44.66% in 2024-25). The customer base is concentrated in NHAI, MoRTH, state irrigation and highway departments and municipal corporations, so a single-client or single-state policy shift transmits directly to revenue.
- Regulatory and contractual sanction risk from project quality failures — BRSR Principle 1 discloses that NHAI issued a show cause notice to KNR Ramanattukara Infra Private Limited and to KNR Constructions Limited over failure of the main carriageway, service road and associated structures in a project stretch, with associated temporary suspension and debarment proceedings. It was settled with an undertaking to construct a viaduct at the subsidiary's own cost and to abstain from NHAI bids for a period, demonstrating that quality lapses can translate into a bidding ban on the Company's largest client.
- Workforce attrition, concentrated in site workers — BRSR Section A reports permanent worker turnover of 104.54% in 2025-26, up from 46.50% in 2024-25, and permanent employee turnover of 10.01% against 0.57% the prior year. For a business whose stated moat is in-house resource control and execution to schedule, a doubling of worker churn is a structural risk to the delivery record.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: KNRCL's expansion in 2025-26 was project-led rather than plant-led: it is a construction services business with no manufacturing plants (BRSR Section A records 0 plants and 32 offices, all national). The largest step was entry into commercial mining. The Company received a Letter of Acceptance from Patratu Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (a JV of NTPC and Jharkhand Bijli Vitran Nigam) to develop and operate the Banhardih Coal Mining Block in Jharkhand, a project valued at Rs 48,006 Mn of which KNRCL's portion is 74%; the block received Stage-I (F1) forest clearance during the year, which permits site work to begin and moves the project from award to execution. It is held through the 74%-owned subsidiary KNRHC Baidyanath Banhardih Coal Mine Private Limited. A second mining LoA followed, for a Rs 33,662 Mn (excluding GST) coal mining and overburden removal project from Southeastern Coalfields Limited at Kusmunda OCP, Chhattisgarh, to be executed over eight years in joint venture with Sushee Infra & Mining Limited. On roads, the Company secured a Letter of Award for an NHAI HAM four-laning of NH-167 from Gudebellur to Mahabubnagar in Telangana valued at Rs 17,340.0 Mn, incorporating KNR Manyamkonda Infra Private Limited as the project subsidiary, and a Rs 21,630.0 Mn HAM project from the Tamil Nadu State Highways Authority for a four-lane elevated corridor along the East Coast Road, incorporating KNR Mahabalipuram Infra Private Limited. It also won a Rs 4,591 Mn GHMC package for multi-level flyovers and grade separators at the Khajaguda and IIIT junctions, and a Rs 3,192 Mn EPC iconic bridge across Mir Alam Tank for Musi Riverfront Development Corporation Limited. Completions during the year included Provisional Certificates of Completion for the Ramanattukara-Valanchery and Valanchery-Kappirikkad Kerala HAM stretches (effective July 2025) and for Chittor-Thatchur Package 03, a Certificate of Completion for the elevated highway along Avinashi Road in Coimbatore from Goldwins to Uppilipalayam, and completion of the Oddanchatram-Madathukulam project. In irrigation the Company is executing a 4 x 90 MW pump house in Telangana. Capital is being recycled rather than added: Share Purchase Agreements were executed to sell 100% of four HAM SPVs (KNR Palani, KNR Ramagiri, KNR Guruvayur, KNR Ramanattukara) to Indus Infra Trust for an expected total consideration of Rs 15,432 Mn, with the process expected to complete by September 2026; the Palani and Ramagiri transfers have already closed. Forward-looking expansion is directed at metro rail, railway infrastructure, solar EPC leveraging existing land banks, and AI-enabled data centre infrastructure, where model MoUs for power-assured Agentic AI data centre development are being advanced. Note on routing: most of the project detail above sits in the Corporate Overview, MD&A and MD/ED letters bundled to the profile, strategy_outlook and risks_esg prompts rather than in the capex bundle, which carried mainly macro industry commentary.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record Rs 12.22 Lakh Crores to capital expenditure, an 11.5% increase over the Revised Estimates for 2025-26, which management reads as sustaining demand across transportation, mining, water infrastructure and specialised sectors
- Road awards slowed through the year because authorities are now clearing land and settling approvals before they tender; management notes this delays the award but shortens the execution that follows, and industry order inflows moderated as a result while work already awarded continued at pace
- National highway construction activity declined in 2025-26 and, per the CARE Report, is expected to moderate further in 2026-27, from around 25 km per day to 21-22 km per day, on subdued awarding, execution challenges and heightened competitive intensity
- MoRTH shortened the material price adjustment cycle from three months to one month during the year, which management says gives contractors better sight of input costs and enables faster pass-through of material and equipment cost fluctuations
- Revenue and margins moderated over the year, reflecting a slower awarding cycle across the roads sector, the completion of higher-margin irrigation work, and the absence of arbitration income of the kind recognised in the previous year; management's medium-term focus is on recovering margins
- Working capital improved, with net working capital down to 78 days from 93 days
- CRISIL reaffirmed the long-term bank facilities rating at CRISIL AA/Stable and the short-term rating at CRISIL A1+ in February 2026, removing both from Rating Watch with Developing Implications, which management cites as an enabler of bidding capacity
- Government policy tailwinds in mining (National Critical Mineral Mission, MMDR Amendment Act 2025), railways and metro (seven High-Speed Rail corridors, metro network at 1,155 km across 26 cities) and urban water (AMRUT 2.0) are cited as opening the adjacent markets the Company is targeting
- All ongoing projects are located across South and East India, where the Company's established operational base and regional presence support efficient execution
- Order book stood at Rs 86,725 Mn as on March 31, 2026, described by management as diversified and balanced across project types and funding sources
- Including projects awarded April to June 2026 and those where LoAs have been issued, the executable order book rose to Rs 1,52,340 Mn as on June 30, 2026, spread across four segments and seven states
- Segment mix of the March 2026 order book: mining 41%, irrigation 19%, road HAM 16%, other road projects 14%, pipeline 10%
- Funding mix of the March 2026 order book: Central Government around 43%, State Government around 39%, captive HAM projects 16%
- The Directors' Report states the order book provides execution visibility of around 1.5 to 2 years excluding the mining project, which is to be executed over a period of six years
- Eight HAM projects with a total bid cost of Rs 96,188 Mn have been executed or are in the road portfolio
- Mining contributes approximately 30% of the executable order book per the Corporate Overview segment note
- New wins during and after the year include the Banhardih coal block (Rs 48,005.7 Mn, KNRCL portion 74%), Kusmunda OCP coal mining and overburden removal (Rs 33,662 Mn ex-GST, in JV with Sushee Infra & Mining), an NHAI HAM four-laning of NH-167 Gudebellur to Mahabubnagar (Rs 17,340.0 Mn), a TANSHA HAM elevated corridor along the East Coast Road (Rs 21,630.0 Mn), a GHMC flyover and grade separator package at Khajaguda and IIIT junctions (Rs 4,591 Mn) and an iconic bridge across Mir Alam Tank for Musi Riverfront Development Corporation (Rs 3,192 Mn)

risks.risk: Margin compression from intense competitive bidding
risks.note: Intense competition in the infrastructure sector has prompted aggressive bidding at lower prices to secure new orders, and management states the highly competitive environment has compressed EBITDA margins compared with historical levels. The Threats column of the SCOT analysis names a highly competitive bidding landscape that forces lower pricing, impacting sustainable margins and growth.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility in bitumen and petroleum-linked inputs
risks.note: Global geopolitical tensions can trigger sharp increases in crude oil prices, driving up the cost of bitumen and other petroleum-based construction inputs, creating uncertainty in project cost management and affecting profitability. Mitigation rests on the revised MoRTH price adjustment mechanism, which shortens the adjustment cycle from three months to one month and enables faster pass-through.

risks.risk: Liquidity strain and capital concentration in completed assets
risks.note: Large infrastructure projects require substantial upfront equity investment, pressuring liquidity if capital is not recycled efficiently, and excess capital tied up in completed assets limits the ability to pursue new and diversified opportunities. The response is asset monetisation through divestment of completed HAM assets to infrastructure trusts and reinvestment of proceeds into the order book.

risks.risk: Dependence on the pace of government project awarding
risks.note: National highway construction activity declined during 2025-26 and, per the CARE Report cited in the MD&A, is expected to moderate further in 2026-27, from around 25 km per day to 21-22 km per day, on subdued project awarding. Fewer road projects came to tender than in any recent season and management states the year's results reflect that shortfall, so revenue is directly exposed to a policy-driven awarding cycle the Company does not control.

BRSR Section A records a single business activity, Construction and Engineering, at 100% of turnover, with exports at 0.00% and operations in seven states, all ongoing projects located across South and East India. one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: KNR Constructions is a 30-year-old Indian EPC infrastructure developer that has extended from highways into irrigation, urban corridors and commercial coal mining, with an order book of Rs 86,725 Mn as on March 31, 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KNRCL designs and builds national highways, expressways, flyovers and state highways under EPC, HAM and BOT modes, alongside reservoirs, lift irrigation schemes, pump houses and urban water systems, and elevated corridors, grade separators and utility infrastructure for cities. More recently it has entered commercial mining, providing mine development, excavation and overburden removal services. Its clients are almost entirely government bodies - NHAI, MoRTH, state highway and irrigation departments, municipal corporations and public-sector undertakings - with exports at 0.00% of turnover.

- Road awards slowed through the year because authorities are now clearing land and settling approvals before they tender; management notes this delays the award but shortens the execution that follows, and industry order inflows moderated as a result while work already awarded continued at pace
- National highway construction activity declined in 2025-26 and, per the CARE Report, is expected to moderate further in 2026-27, from around 25 km per day to 21-22 km per day, on subdued awarding, execution challenges and heightened competitive intensity
- MoRTH shortened the material price adjustment cycle from three months to one month during the year, which management says gives contractors better sight of input costs and enables faster pass-through of material and equipment cost fluctuations
- Revenue and margins moderated over the year, reflecting a slower awarding cycle across the roads sector, the completion of higher-margin irrigation work, and the absence of arbitration income of the kind recognised in the previous year; management's medium-term focus is on recovering margins
- Working capital improved, with net working capital down to 78 days from 93 days
- CRISIL reaffirmed the long-term bank facilities rating at CRISIL AA/Stable and the short-term rating at CRISIL A1+ in February 2026, removing both from Rating Watch with Developing Implications, which management cites as an enabler of bidding capacity
- Government policy tailwinds in mining (National Critical Mineral Mission, MMDR Amendment Act 2025), railways and metro (seven High-Speed Rail corridors, metro network at 1,155 km across 26 cities) and urban water (AMRUT 2.0) are cited as opening the adjacent markets the Company is targeting
- All ongoing projects are located across South and East India, where the Company's established operational base and regional presence support efficient execution
- Order book stood at Rs 86,725 Mn as on March 31, 2026, described by management as diversified and balanced across project types and funding sources
- Including projects awarded April to June 2026 and those where LoAs have been issued, the executable order book rose to Rs 1,52,340 Mn as on June 30, 2026, spread across four segments and seven states
- Segment mix of the March 2026 order book: mining 41%, irrigation 19%, road HAM 16%, other road projects 14%, pipeline 10%
- Funding mix of the March 2026 order book: Central Government around 43%, State Government around 39%, captive HAM projects 16%
- The Directors' Report states the order book provides execution visibility of around 1.5 to 2 years excluding the mining project, which is to be executed over a period of six years
- Eight HAM projects with a total bid cost of Rs 96,188 Mn have been executed or are in the road portfolio
- Mining contributes approximately 30% of the executable order book per the Corporate Overview segment note
- New wins during and after the year include the Banhardih coal block (Rs 48,005.7 Mn, KNRCL portion 74%), Kusmunda OCP coal mining and overburden removal (Rs 33,662 Mn ex-GST, in JV with Sushee Infra & Mining), an NHAI HAM four-laning of NH-167 Gudebellur to Mahabubnagar (Rs 17,340.0 Mn), a TANSHA HAM elevated corridor along the East Coast Road (Rs 21,630.0 Mn), a GHMC flyover and grade separator package at Khajaguda and IIIT junctions (Rs 4,591 Mn) and an iconic bridge across Mir Alam Tank for Musi Riverfront Development Corporation (Rs 3,192 Mn)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: KNRCL's expansion in 2025-26 was project-led rather than plant-led: it is a construction services business with no manufacturing plants (BRSR Section A records 0 plants and 32 offices, all national). The largest step was entry into commercial mining. The Company received a Letter of Acceptance from Patratu Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (a JV of NTPC and Jharkhand Bijli Vitran Nigam) to develop and operate the Banhardih Coal Mining Block in Jharkhand, a project valued at Rs 48,006 Mn of which KNRCL's portion is 74%; the block received Stage-I (F1) forest clearance during the year, which permits site work to begin and moves the project from award to execution. It is held through the 74%-owned subsidiary KNRHC Baidyanath Banhardih Coal Mine Private Limited. A second mining LoA followed, for a Rs 33,662 Mn (excluding GST) coal mining and overburden removal project from Southeastern Coalfields Limited at Kusmunda OCP, Chhattisgarh, to be executed over eight years in joint venture with Sushee Infra & Mining Limited. On roads, the Company secured a Letter of Award for an NHAI HAM four-laning of NH-167 from Gudebellur to Mahabubnagar in Telangana valued at Rs 17,340.0 Mn, incorporating KNR Manyamkonda Infra Private Limited as the project subsidiary, and a Rs 21,630.0 Mn HAM project from the Tamil Nadu State Highways Authority for a four-lane elevated corridor along the East Coast Road, incorporating KNR Mahabalipuram Infra Private Limited. It also won a Rs 4,591 Mn GHMC package for multi-level flyovers and grade separators at the Khajaguda and IIIT junctions, and a Rs 3,192 Mn EPC iconic bridge across Mir Alam Tank for Musi Riverfront Development Corporation Limited. Completions during the year included Provisional Certificates of Completion for the Ramanattukara-Valanchery and Valanchery-Kappirikkad Kerala HAM stretches (effective July 2025) and for Chittor-Thatchur Package 03, a Certificate of Completion for the elevated highway along Avinashi Road in Coimbatore from Goldwins to Uppilipalayam, and completion of the Oddanchatram-Madathukulam project. In irrigation the Company is executing a 4 x 90 MW pump house in Telangana. Capital is being recycled rather than added: Share Purchase Agreements were executed to sell 100% of four HAM SPVs (KNR Palani, KNR Ramagiri, KNR Guruvayur, KNR Ramanattukara) to Indus Infra Trust for an expected total consideration of Rs 15,432 Mn, with the process expected to complete by September 2026; the Palani and Ramagiri transfers have already closed. Forward-looking expansion is directed at metro rail, railway infrastructure, solar EPC leveraging existing land banks, and AI-enabled data centre infrastructure, where model MoUs for power-assured Agentic AI data centre development are being advanced. Note on routing: most of the project detail above sits in the Corporate Overview, MD&A and MD/ED letters bundled to the profile, strategy_outlook and risks_esg prompts rather than in the capex bundle, which carried mainly macro industry commentary.

non-obvious takeaways: INR150-200cr of unbilled irrigation revenue expected to be certified in Q3FY26; mining project's INR90cr development phase revenue is non-recurring and will not impact EBITDA margin; asset monetization of 4 HAM assets could reduce net debt by INR500-700cr if closed by Dec 2025

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

hero.oneLiner: KNR Constructions is a 30-year-old Indian EPC infrastructure developer that has extended from highways into irrigation, urban corridors and commercial coal mining, with an order book of Rs 86,725 Mn as on March 31, 2026.
